sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large deciduous tree native from western Asia to the western Himalaya and long cultivated elsewhere. It can reach about 25 m and develops a broad crown.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and nuts
sections.text: The leaves are compound and pinnate with a terminal leaflet. Male flowers form hanging catkins; female flowers develop into a fruit with a green husk enclosing a woody nut 4–6 cm long.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The kernel of the ripe walnut is edible; the outer husk is not the usual food portion.
